title: Kubernetes Events
description:
Kubernetes Warning events and Flux (GitOps) reconciliation state for the four dis-core clusters (AT22, AT23, TT02, PROD), filterable by product. Products are the `product-<name>` namespaces; each one holds its own Flux `Kustomization` and `OCIRepository`, so the *Product* filter narrows both the workload events and the Flux state to one team.

Sources, all pinned to fixed datasource UIDs:
* **Container Insights `KubeEvents`** — one cross-workspace query over the four `dis-core-<env>-aks-law` workspaces (30-day retention), environment derived from `ClusterName`. Only **Warning** events are collected on these clusters, which is what failures are; successful reconciliations and normal scheduling are not recorded.
* **Azure Resource Graph** — the AKS Flux extension's `fluxConfigurations` and their compliance state (current, not historical).
* **kube-state-metrics `gotk_resource_info`** in each `dis-core-<env>-products-amw` — ready / not-ready over time for product Kustomizations.

Kyverno `PolicyViolation` audit events are hidden by default (toggle at the top); they are the large majority of all event rows and almost never about a product. Container Insights writes a row per event update, so every count here is a count of distinct event objects.

links.title: GitOps Flux — Application Deployments
links.tooltip: Flux extension and configuration compliance across all subscriptions (Azure Resource Graph)

list.name: env
list.label: Environment
list.description: dis-core environment; derived from the cluster name in every query.

list.name: product
list.label: Product
list.description: Every `product-<name>` namespace that had pods in the last 7 days or a Warning event in the last 30 days, plus `platform` for all other namespaces. The lookback is fixed in the query (time range: Query), so the list does not shrink when the dashboard range is narrowed.
list.definition:
union
  (KubePodInventory | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) and isnotempty(Namespace) | distinct Namespace),
  (KubeEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) and isnotempty(Namespace) | distinct Namespace)
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| distinct Product
| order by Product asc

azureLogAnalytics.query:
union
  (KubePodInventory | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) and isnotempty(Namespace) | distinct Namespace),
  (KubeEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) and isnotempty(Namespace) | distinct Namespace)
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| distinct Product
| order by Product asc

list.name: policy
list.label: Kyverno policy violations
list.description: `hide` drops Kyverno `PolicyViolation` audit events from every panel except the dedicated table in the *Platform* row; they are the large majority of all events and almost never about a product.

panels.title: Warning events — selected range
panels.description: Distinct Kubernetes **Warning** events per environment in the selected time range, for the selected products. Kyverno `PolicyViolation` audit events are excluded unless the *Kyverno policy violations* toggle is set to `show`. Only Warning events are collected on these clusters (Container Insights `collect_all_kube_events` is off), so Normal events such as successful scheduling or a completed reconciliation never appear here.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
let envs = datatable(Env: string) ["AT22", "AT23", "TT02", "PROD"]
| where Env in ($env);
envs
| join kind=leftouter (
    base
    | summarize Events = dcount(EventKey) by Env
  ) on Env
| project Env, Events = coalesce(Events, 0)
| extend EnvOrder = case(Env == "AT22", 1, Env == "AT23", 2, Env == "TT02", 3, Env == "PROD", 4, 9)
| order by EnvOrder asc
| project Env, Events

panels.title: Flux failures — selected range
panels.description: Distinct Warning events on Flux objects (`Kustomization`, `OCIRepository`, `HelmRelease`, …) per environment: `ReconciliationFailed`, `HealthCheckFailed`, `OCIArtifactPullFailed` and status-update errors. Green means no reconciliation failed in the range. The events themselves, with their messages, are in the *GitOps / Flux* row.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
let envs = datatable(Env: string) ["AT22", "AT23", "TT02", "PROD"]
| where Env in ($env);
envs
| join kind=leftouter (
    base
    | where ObjectKind in ("Kustomization", "HelmRelease", "HelmChart", "HelmRepository", "OCIRepository", "GitRepository", "Bucket")
    | summarize Events = dcount(EventKey) by Env
  ) on Env
| project Env, Events = coalesce(Events, 0)
| extend EnvOrder = case(Env == "AT22", 1, Env == "AT23", 2, Env == "TT02", 3, Env == "PROD", 4, 9)
| order by EnvOrder asc
| project Env, Events

panels.title: Non-compliant Flux configurations — now
panels.description: Current state, not history: the number of AKS Flux-extension configurations per environment whose `complianceState` is not `Compliant`, read from Azure Resource Graph. dis-core runs Flux as the AKS extension, so every platform component and every product `syncroot` is one such configuration. A non-zero value here is the single clearest sign that GitOps is stuck; the table below names the object and the reason. Scoped by the *Product* filter exactly like the table, and a configuration counts once however many of its objects are failing; `Pending`, `Suspended` and `Unknown` count as not compliant, an empty state does not.

azureResourceGraph.query:
kubernetesconfigurationresources
| where type =~ "microsoft.kubernetesconfiguration/fluxconfigurations"
| extend Cluster = tostring(split(tolower(id), "/")[8])
| where Cluster startswith "dis-core-"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, Cluster))
| where Env in ($env)
| mv-expand status = properties.statuses
| extend Namespace = tostring(status.namespace), State = tostring(status.complianceState)
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Product in ($product)
| summarize NonCompliant = dcountif(name, isnotempty(State) and State !~ "Compliant") by Env
| extend EnvOrder = case(Env == "AT22", 1, Env == "AT23", 2, Env == "TT02", 3, Env == "PROD", 4, 9)
| order by EnvOrder asc
| project Env, NonCompliant

panels.title: Non-compliant Flux configurations — current state (Azure Resource Graph)
panels.description: One row per Flux object that the AKS Flux extension reports as not compliant right now, with the extension's own message (for example `health check failed … Job/…/migrate-database status: 'Failed'` or `dependency '…/pre-deployment' is not ready`). `Configuration` is the Azure `fluxConfiguration` name; product configurations are named `<product>-<4 chars>` and live in the `product-<product>` namespace. Empty means everything is reconciled. This is a live snapshot from Resource Graph and is not affected by the dashboard time range.

azureResourceGraph.query:
kubernetesconfigurationresources
| where type =~ "microsoft.kubernetesconfiguration/fluxconfigurations"
| extend Cluster = tostring(split(tolower(id), "/")[8])
| where Cluster startswith "dis-core-"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, Cluster))
| where Env in ($env)
| mv-expand status = properties.statuses
| extend Namespace = tostring(status.namespace), State = tostring(status.complianceState)
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Product in ($product)
| where isnotempty(State) and State !~ "Compliant"
| project Env, Product, Configuration = name, Kind = tostring(status.kind), Object = tostring(status.name), State, Message = tostring(status.message), Updated = todatetime(properties.statusUpdatedAt)
| order by Env asc, Configuration asc

panels.title: Product Flux Kustomizations — ready state over time
panels.description: Ready / reconciling / not-ready bands for every Flux `Kustomization` in a `product-*` namespace, one query per environment against that environment's `dis-core-<env>-products-amw` (kube-state-metrics `gotk_resource_info`, where the object's namespace is in `exported_namespace`). Red blocks are the periods the AKS Flux extension would also have reported as non-compliant; a gap means kube-state-metrics stopped reporting the object, which is a different failure. Platform-level Kustomizations (`platform-system`, `flux-system`) are deliberately not on this timeline; their failures show up in the table above and in the events feed below.

targets.expr:
(max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="false"}) * 2)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="unknown"}) * 1)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="true"}) * 0)

(max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="false"}) * 2)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="unknown"}) * 1)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="true"}) * 0)

(max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="false"}) * 2)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="unknown"}) * 1)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="true"}) * 0)

(max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="false"}) * 2)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="unknown"}) * 1)
or (max by (cluster, exported_namespace, name) (gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="kustomization", cluster=~"(?i)^dis-core-${env:regex}-aks$", exported_namespace=~"^product-${product:regex}$", ready="true"}) * 0)

panels.title: Flux warning events
panels.description: Every Warning event emitted by the Flux controllers on `Kustomization`, `OCIRepository`, `HelmRelease`, `HelmChart`, `HelmRepository`, `GitRepository` and `Bucket` objects, newest first, deduplicated to one row per event object with its latest message. `Count` is the Kubernetes event count (how many times the same event recurred), so a single row with a high count is a failure that kept repeating. Typical reasons: `ReconciliationFailed` (a manifest was rejected, often by an admission webhook), `HealthCheckFailed` (the Kustomization applied but a Deployment or Job never became healthy), `OCIArtifactPullFailed` (the registry was unreachable).

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
base
| where ObjectKind in ("Kustomization", "HelmRelease", "HelmChart", "HelmRepository", "OCIRepository", "GitRepository", "Bucket")
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, Message, Count) by Env, Product, Namespace, ObjectKind, Name, Reason, FirstSeen
| project TimeGenerated, Env, Product, Kind = ObjectKind, Name, Reason, Count = toint(Count), Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 300

panels.title: Workloads — pods, replica sets, jobs, autoscalers
Workload warning events per interval, by reason
panels.description: Distinct Warning events on Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, CronJobs and HorizontalPodAutoscalers, stacked by reason. Read it as *what kind of trouble, when*: `BackOff` and `Unhealthy` are the app crashing or failing its probes, `FailedScheduling` and `FailedMount`/`FailedAttachVolume` are the platform not being able to place or start the pod, `FailedGetResourceMetric` is an autoscaler that cannot read metrics (usually harmless noise from pods without resource requests).

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
base
| where ObjectKind in ("Pod", "ReplicaSet", "Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Job", "CronJob", "HorizontalPodAutoscaler")
| summarize Events = dcount(EventKey) by Reason, bin(TimeGenerated, $__interval)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

panels.title: Objects with the most warning events
panels.description: Which workloads are generating the warnings, with the set of reasons seen and the time of the last one. A pod that is high on this list with `BackOff` is crash-looping; a ReplicaSet with `FailedCreate` is being blocked by an admission policy or a quota.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
base
| where ObjectKind in ("Pod", "ReplicaSet", "Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Job", "CronJob", "HorizontalPodAutoscaler")
| summarize Events = dcount(EventKey), Reasons = strcat_array(make_set(Reason, 5), ", "), Last = max(TimeGenerated) by Env, Product, Kind = ObjectKind, Name
| top 30 by Events desc

panels.title: Latest workload warning events
panels.description: Newest workload Warning events first, one row per event object with its latest message. Use the `Product` and `Env` filters at the top to narrow this to one team's namespace in one environment; the built-in column filters narrow further.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")

base
| where ObjectKind in ("Pod", "ReplicaSet", "Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Job", "CronJob", "HorizontalPodAutoscaler")

| project TimeGenerated, Env, Product, Kind = ObjectKind, Name, Reason, Count = toint(Count), Message

panels.title: Node warning events per interval, by reason
panels.description: Warning events on `Node` objects: `FreezeScheduled` and `VMEventScheduled` are Azure maintenance notices from the node-problem-detector, `Drain` and `Rebooted` are node upgrades or repairs, `CoreDNSUnreachable`, `IMDSUnreachable` and `UnbalancedIRQs` are host-level health checks. A burst across many nodes at once is usually a cluster upgrade.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
base
| where ObjectKind == "Node"
| summarize Events = dcount(EventKey) by Reason, bin(TimeGenerated, $__interval)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

panels.title: Operator and controller errors
panels.description: Warning events on everything that is neither a workload, a Flux object nor a Node — mostly Azure Service Operator resources (`PrivateDnsZone`, `FlexibleServers*`, `RoleAssignment`, `UserAssignedIdentity`, `FederatedIdentityCredential`), `ExternalSecret` sync failures and other operators. Grouped by kind and reason with the latest message, so a product's failing infrastructure dependency is visible even when its pods look fine.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
base
| where ObjectKind !in ("Pod", "ReplicaSet", "Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Job", "CronJob", "HorizontalPodAutoscaler") and ObjectKind !in ("Kustomization", "HelmRelease", "HelmChart", "HelmRepository", "OCIRepository", "GitRepository", "Bucket") and ObjectKind != "Node"
| summarize Events = dcount(EventKey), Objects = dcount(Name), arg_max(TimeGenerated, Message) by Env, Product, Kind = ObjectKind, Reason, SourceComponent
| project Env, Product, Kind, Reason, SourceComponent, Events, Objects, Last = TimeGenerated, LastMessage = Message
| top 40 by Events desc

panels.title: Kyverno policy violations by policy or object
panels.description: Counted regardless of the *Kyverno policy violations* toggle. Rows are raw event rows, not distinct events, because Kyverno re-emits the same audit violation on every background scan. Rows on `ClusterPolicy` objects name the policy (`disallow-host-path`, `disallow-host-namespaces`, …) and are almost entirely about `kube-system` system workloads such as the cilium operator; they make up the large majority of the Kubernetes events ingested from prod. Rows on `Pod`/`ReplicaSet`/`Deployment` objects are the same violations attributed to the workload.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
KubeEvents
| where Reason == "PolicyViolation"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| summarize Rows = count(), Objects = dcount(strcat(Namespace, "|", Name)), Last = max(TimeGenerated) by Env, Kind = ObjectKind, PolicyOrObject = Name
| top 30 by Rows desc

panels.title: Event stream — deduplicated, newest first
panels.description: Everything that passed the filters at the top, one row per Kubernetes event object with its latest message, `FirstSeen`/`LastSeen` from the event itself and `Count` as the number of recurrences. Capped at 500 rows; narrow the time range or the filters if the cap is hit. The column filters and the inspector (panel menu → Inspect → Data) work on this table.

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let base = KubeEvents
| where Reason != "PolicyViolation" or "$policy" == "show"
| extend Env = toupper(extract("dis-core-(\\w+)-aks", 1, ClusterName))
| extend Product = iff(Namespace startswith "product-", substring(Namespace, 8), "platform")
| where Env in ($env) and Product in ($product)
| extend EventKey = strcat(ClusterName, "|", Namespace, "|", ObjectKind, "|", Name, "|", Reason, "|", tostring(FirstSeen));
base
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, Message, Count, LastSeen, SourceComponent) by Env, Product, Namespace, ObjectKind, Name, Reason, FirstSeen
| project TimeGenerated, Env, Product, Namespace, Kind = ObjectKind, Name, Reason, Count = toint(Count), SourceComponent, FirstSeen, LastSeen, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 500
